messages:
acme_ops: Hey team — we're seeing a new error in production after the recent SDK upgrade. Calls to our create_order tool are failing with "failed to parse function arguments: invalid JSON". Happened ~11:23AM PT. Example assistant response pasted below.

acme_ops: ```json
{"name":"create_order","arguments":"{\"items\": [{\"id\": \"123\", \"qty\":1}], \"customer_id\": \"ACME-1\"}"}
```

jessica: Thanks — can you paste the request you sent and the declared function schema? Also which SDK+version and model?

acme_ops: Request was a standard openai-style call via our middleware (we upgraded to sdk-js v2.4.0). Model: gpt-4o-mini. Function schema below:

acme_ops: ```json
{"name":"create_order","parameters": {"type":"object","properties":{"items":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"id":{"type":"string"},"qty":{"type":"integer"}}}},"customer_id":{"type":"string"}},"required":["items","customer_id"]}}
```

samir: Looking at the assistant response you pasted: the assistant returned a field "arguments" that is a string containing JSON (double-encoded). The runtime expects a parsed object for arguments. That will trigger "invalid JSON" during runtime parse.

mike: We recently tightened the parser to reject stringified arguments instead of attempting to parse them. The SDK change plus gpt-4o-mini's tendency to wrap may cause this. Repro: if assistant returns arguments as a JSON string rather than a JSON object, our parse pipeline fails with a 400 and message shown.

acme_ops: Repro steps I used:

acme_ops: ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model":"gpt-4o-mini",
    "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"create order for 123 x1"}],
    "functions":[{"name":"create_order","parameters":{...}}],
    "function_call":{"name":"create_order"}
  }'
```

jessica: Thanks — quick mitigation: pin the model to gpt-4o or set the conversation "function_call":{"name":"create_order"} and enable the SDK option "parse_stringified_arguments":true (client-side workaround) while we patch runtime to attempt a safe JSON parse of string arguments.

samir: Filing infra ticket to add tolerant parsing that will attempt JSON.parse on string arguments and validate against the schema. If parse succeeds we accept, else return clear error to the caller. Ticket: INF-7124.

infra-bot: INF-7124 created by samir. ETA: 48h for a patch on staging.

mike: For immediate customer relief, ask acme_ops to downgrade to sdk-js v2.3.1 or to add the client workaround. Also please send the exact failing full payload to support@redwood so we can repro with their account context.

acme_ops: Will try the downgrade and send the payload. Thanks everyone :pray:

jessica: Following up — once you send the payload we'll escalate to oncall if the workaround fails. cc @mike
